scope: Run71 typed first-nonfinite probe only; no build/test/device/model/cleanup.

compile_guard_equivalence.operation: In-memory LF-normalized removal of all 28 complete #if defined(STRATA_PREFILL_FINITE_PROBE) blocks from E71 src/prefill/prefill.cpp, with nested preprocessor depth preserved.

default_guards.runtime_request: requested() accepts only the exact string 1 (finite_probe.hpp:10-12); detail parsing occurs only while probe_enabled (prefill.cpp:2056-2064).
default_guards.detail_selection: Absent STRATA_PREFILL_DETAIL_LAYER sets -1; strict decimal/range parsing is finite_probe.hpp:14-29. Detail calls also require allocated probe and exact layer match (prefill.cpp:2575-2584).

typed_classifier_and_record.classification: f32 uses exponent mask 0x7f800000; f16 uses 0x7c00; bf16 uses 0x7f80. Magnitude below infinity is finite, equal is infinity, above is NaN; sign selects +/-Inf. This matches IEEE encodings for the declared formats.
typed_classifier_and_record.first_record: Same-stream scan kernels serialize checkpoints. Each kernel atomically claims ordinal from zero; only the claiming ordinal contributes min index and complete NaN/+Inf/-Inf counters. Later scans return after seeing an earlier ordinal. The record is copied only after an existing stream synchronization; point fields are written before kernel completion.
typed_classifier_and_record.coordinates: row_offset must be nonnegative; serialized source_row=row_offset+index/width, row and column are scan-relative, and expert defaults -1. Per-expert fallback scans set expert=e; grouped MMQ scans leave expert=-1.

producer_and_shape_review.checked: m.mixed is scanned after gr_mix/gr_mix_r; m.mixed_h is hf(s) FP16 and m.mixed_bf/mixed_bf_lo are CUDA BF16 images. Typed flags f16/bf16 and [T,N] match producers.
logits [T,E] scanned after bf16_proj and before route; weights [T,K] scanned after route on same stream.
sgate/sup [T,640] after projections; sh_h [T,640] f16 after swiglu_pair and before shared down; shared [T,N] and sg [T,1] after their producers.

GU scan uses m.GU+r0*1280 with nr rows; H scan uses m.H+r0*640 with the same nr/r0, after swiglu and before quantize. Down writes Dm at r0*N. Buffers are FP32 here; GU/H offsets and extents match Product destinations.

Xs is gathered from m.mixed_h into expert order using src_dev; scan Xs+o0*N covers ne x N. dq_gu is dequantized FP16 [1280,N], dq_d FP16 [N,640], each scanned with expert=e. GU [ne,1280] and Hh f16 [ne,640] use o0 offsets; scans sit after producers and before SwiGLU/down consumers.

CPU share requires !m.pp (3033-3034), so CPU tail rows do not coexist with peer path. back_at=rows_local after peer-row partition; in peer_sums mode peer rows are accumulated separately and absent from Dm, so scan of [0,back_at) is correct. Otherwise scan T*K rows after CPU H2D and peer waits/copies.

moe_path_record.fields: native=lay.native; mmq=use_mmq; fused=fused_l; gu/down types from selected layer layout; stream_all/peer/peer_sums and cpu_rows are passed at the per-selected-layer site.
moe_path_record.interpretation: Flags are descriptive predicates, not a one-hot enum: use_mmq may be 1 together with fused=1 because the fused eligibility depends on MMQ planning. The record is emitted only for the selected layer.
moe_path_record.atomic_log_line: moe_path and checkpoint each use one fprintf call plus fflush (finite_probe.cu:117-125,153-156); report_after_sync formats first_bad into a bounded local buffer then emits one JSON line, avoiding the old two-call split.

potential_issues_or_limits.detail: route_weights is scanned immediately after route, before optional STRATA_DBG_ROUTE_OVERRIDE can replace m.ids/m.w. If override is enabled simultaneously, the diagnostic describes original route weights rather than the values consumed downstream. Not applicable when that hook is absent; current source metadata alone does not prove its runtime environment.

MMQ scans cover a group of experts and set no expert id; report_moe_path records total expert count/types but not order/group bounds. row_offset/source_row correctly identify packed expert-order coordinates, but a first_bad record alone cannot name the member expert in a multi-expert group.
A consumer must not interpret mmq/fused as mutually exclusive labels; they are use_mmq and fused_l predicates and can both be true. The JSON currently does not name these semantics explicitly.
